body.statement: When \(s=c=1\), the compatible-root formula reduces to the fixed-clean-margin binary odds reconstruction of ZhangNieSoonLiu2013. When additionally \(\theta_L=\theta_U=1\), it reduces to \(b=p_1(1-p_0)\). For the synthetic box \(q_0=1/5\), \(q_1=3/10\), \(u\in[1/20,1/10]\), \(v\in[4/5,9/10]\), \(\theta\in[1,4]\), and \(\kappa\le7/10\), the endpoints are \((\sqrt{193}-5)/48\) and \(4/15\), both attained by positive-cell laws.
body.justification: Known-case collapse and an exact nondegenerate witness guard the candidate algebra against sign and root-selection errors.
body.gap: The clean-assay reductions are prior art; the exact uncertain-assay witness is a diagnostic specialization of the new envelope rather than an independent novelty claim.
body.consumer: The exact values provide regression tests for a certified implementation and a transparent worked example for trial analysts.
body.proof_tex:
If \(s=c=1\), then \(u=0\), \(v=1\), and assay inversion gives \(p_a=q_a\).  Substitution in the unique quadratic therefore gives the fixed-clean-margin binary odds reconstruction.  If also \(\theta_L=\theta_U=1\), then \(r=0\), and the unique-root formula becomes
\[
 b=p_1(1-p_0).
\]

For the stated synthetic box, \(u\leq1/10<q_0<q_1<4/5\leq v\), and the smallest possible channel difference is \(4/5-1/10=7/10\).  Thus every point of the rectangle is feasible whenever \(\kappa\leq7/10\), and the informativeness cut is redundant.  At \(\theta=4\), the stationary-line sums are
\[
 q_0+q_1\pm2|q_1-q_0|=\frac{3}{10},\frac{7}{10},
\]
both below the rectangle's minimum sum \(1/20+4/5=17/20\).  Hence the lower endpoint is found by checking the four vertices.  In lexicographic order
\[
 (u,v)\in\{(1/20,4/5),(1/20,9/10),(1/10,4/5),(1/10,9/10)\},
\]
their \(\theta=4\) root values are
\[
 -\frac1{10}+\frac{\sqrt{89}}{30},\qquad
 \frac{10}{51},\qquad
 -\frac2{21}+\frac{2\sqrt{10}}{21},\qquad
 \frac{\sqrt{193}-5}{48}.
\]
Squaring after moving the positive rational terms to the other side verifies that the last is no larger than each of the first three.  Thus the smallest value occurs at \((u,v)=(1/10,9/10)\), where
\[
 p_0=\frac18,qquad p_1=\frac14,qquad
 96b^2+20b-7=0.
\]
The unique feasible root is therefore
\[
 L=\frac{\sqrt{193}-5}{48}.
\]
At \(\theta=1\), the stationary-line sums are \(2q_0=2/5\) and \(2q_1=3/5\), again below the rectangle.  In the same order, the four vertex values are
\[
 \frac4{15},\qquad\frac{70}{289},\qquad\frac{12}{49},\qquad\frac7{32}.
\]
Cross multiplication shows that \(4/15\) is the largest.  It occurs at \((u,v)=(1/20,4/5)\), where \(p_0=1/5\), \(p_1=1/3\), and hence
\[
 U=p_1(1-p_0)=\frac4{15}.
\]
The corresponding cell vectors, in \((00,01,10,11)\) order, are
\[
 \left(\frac{47-\sqrt{193}}{48},
       \frac{\sqrt{193}-5}{48},
       \frac{\sqrt{193}-11}{48},
       \frac{17-\sqrt{193}}{48}\right)
\]
and
\[
 \left(\frac8{15},\frac4{15},\frac2{15},\frac1{15}\right).
\]
Since \(11<\sqrt{193}<14<17\), every displayed cell is positive.  Direct multiplication verifies the respective cross-product equalities at \(\theta=4\) and \(\theta=1\), so both bounds are attained by positive-cell laws.
